newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian state to hold on longer to oil firm stakes.
newsitem.headline: Russian state to hold on longer to oil firm stakes.

text.p: The Russian government will retain state stakes in many companies in the oil and energy sector until the end of 1998 and draw up new rules for managing state stakes in oil companies held in trust under the shares-for-loans programme, the official government bulletin said on Tuesday.

The bulletin published a government decree dated November 23, which strengthens national economic security in the energy sector and implements a decree issued by President Boris Yeltsin in September on retaining state stakes in oil companies.

The decree did not list the oil companies in which stakes will be retained until the end of 1998. But a government spokeswoman said a 23-page list of companies affected included the following companies:

NK LUKoil, Slavneft, Vostochno-Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (East Siberian Oil Co), Vostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Eastern Oil Co), Orenburgskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Onako), NK KomiTEK, Sibirsko-Uralskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibur), Transneft, NK Rosneft, Tyumenskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Tyumen Oil Co), NK Norsi-Oil.
The decree names Russia's biggest oil companies -- LUKoil, YUKOS, Surgutneftegaz, Sidanko and Sibneft -- as the companies in which shares are held in trust under the shares-for-loans scheme.

Under the terms of the shares-for-loans scheme, in which state stakes in partly privatised companies were transferred to investors in return for loans to the government, auction winners were able to sell the shares after September 1.
Spokesmen at LUKoil, YUKOS and the Energy Ministry were not immediately able to comment on the decree.
It was not clear how the decree would affect a number of recently announced plans affecting oil company shares.
Bank Menatep, winner of a shares-for-loans auction in YUKOS, is accepting bids until December 20 for a 33.3 percent stake in YUKOS.
LUKoil has said it may place 15 percent of its shares on the New York Stock Exchange next year to raise $1 billion.
